newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia's Tallinna Pank begins private banking.
newsitem.headline: Estonia's Tallinna Pank begins private banking.

text.p: Estonia's fourth-largest bank, Tallinna Pank, became on Monday one of the first banks in the country to launch private banking, aimed at wealthy people, its chairman Rait Lukas said.

He told a news conference he foresaw two types of client: those with a monthly gross income of 30,000 kroons (around $3,000) who would like a loan of around one million kroons or people who had funds of around 200,000 kroons to invest.
He said that the bank expected to have around 300 clients for the new service.
Having overcome a crisis in 1992, Estonian banks are rated as the most advanced in the Baltic states. All of the top five are traded on the Tallinn stock exchange.
Leading bank Hansapank recently bought a bank in neighbouring Latvia and Tallinna Pank is expected to open an office in Latvia soon.
"Estonia's rapid development is providing more stable income and makes private banking possible," said Tallinna Pank's retail banking division director Raul Parusk.
